3. Defendant No.1 (predecessor of the respondents) contested the suit by filing a written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that Amud Molla was the owner of the suit land but it was wrongly recorded in the names of Sarabdi and others in elmali. Sarabdi and Dabaru never possessed the land. Amud Molla sold the suit land to Bakhar Molla (father of defendant No.1) on 21.07.1920 by registered kabala in which Gahar Molla (son of Sarabdi Molla) was an attesting witness. During operation of the rent roll the plaintiff unsuccessfully raised objection and as such the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 6. Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1(a)-1(e) made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He submitted that both the Courts below misread, and misunderstood the misconstrued materials on record and consequently failed to comprehend the facts of the case and misapplied the law and came to a wrong decision occasioning miscarriage of justice. He submitted that as a matter of course, the vendors of the plaintiffs had no right to transfer the land In excess of .09 acre according to Exhibit-2 rather the plaintiffs could not furnish any document/instrument or any specific particular in support of their claim. He also submitted Exhibit- 1 demonstrated that Sayed (son of Sarabdi) and Jashim Molla (son of Dabaru Molla) sold .09 acre land out of the suit plot to one Nuki Molla by a kabala dated 12.02.1942 A.D. and further Entaj Ali Molla and Kubbat Ali Molla, sons of Mohan Molla transferred .09 acre of land out of the suit plot to the said Nuki Molla by a kabala dated 08.03.1948 A.D. (vide Exhibit-3) despite, the plaintiffs did not express anything with regard to this prospect in the plaint which appears to be the non-disclosure of material facts. He further stated that the plaintiffs submitted a kabala (Exhibit-5) with a view to show that they had purchased .14 acre of land out of the suit plot from one Most. Habijan Bibi and another from Mohammad Ali on 24.01.1963 but in the plaint, no disclosure was made with regard to any such purchase inasmuch there was no evidence to show with regard to the said two vendors had interest in .14 acre of land to sell the same to the plaintiffs as well as the said exhibit was utterly isolated with the plaint in question. Next, he submitted that the plaintiffs claimed .27½ acre of land out of the suit plot by purchase from Fayezuddin and his 5 other brothers (vide Exhibit-4, a kabala dated 20.11.197) but those six brothers had no saleable interest exceeding .09 acre of land to transfer to the plain-tiffs. Since there having been various co-sharers in the suit property the suit for declaration of title with recovery of possession was not maintainable without prayer for a further relief of partition of the suit property. Hence, the suit was not framed properly and was barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and as such the High Court Division has rightly decided in passing the impugned judgment which is liable Lo be affirmed and the appeal be dismissed. 

 9. On the other hand, admitting the suit property to be the property of Amud Molla defendant No.1 stated in his written statement that it was wrongly recorded in the names of Sarabdi Molla and Dabaru Molla in ejmali and they never possessed the land. The defendant claims that Amud Molla sold the suit land to Bakhar Molla father of defendant No.1 on 21.07.1920 by registered kabala in which Gahar Mona son of Sarabdi Molla was a attesting wit-ness and during operation of the rent-roll survey the plaintiffs unsuccessfully raised objection under section 19A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 11. The points involved in this appeal as stated above have already been dealt with in accordance with law by the High Court Division while passing the impugned judgment and order. 

 12. The High Court Division found that the suit land appertaining to C.S. Plot No.237 containing .55 acre of land as set forth in the plaint was recorded in the names of Dabaru Molla and Sarabdt Molla in the remark column of C.S. Khatian No.32 to be in their possession in 8 annas share each. After the death of Sarabdi Mona it devolved upon his sons namely Gahar Molla, Mohor Molla and Sayed Molla and a daughter who died issueless and as such the aforesaid three sons must have inherited .09 acre of land each. After the death of Gahar Molia his sons namely Hasen Molla, Kazim Molla and two daughters namely Kulsom Bewa and Batashi Bibi inherited .09 acre of land jointly left by their Father. Gahar Molla in the suit land. Exhibit-2 shows that the said Kasen Mona, Kazim Molla and their two sisters transferred their shares to the extent of .09 acre of 1 rind to 6(six) brothers namely, Fayezuddin, Ayezuddin, Tayezuddin, Bahezuddin, Hazrat Ali and Hatem Ali by a kabala dated 02.02.1953 A.D. Thereafter, the said Fayezuddin and his .five other brothers transferred .27 acre of land out of the suit plot by a kabala dated 20.11.1957 to the plaintiffs vide Exhibit-4. In this respect the High Court Division reached to a definite conclusion that although they had no right to transfer the land in excess of .09 acre of land which was purchased by them through Exhibit-2, but they transferred .27V2 acre of land which is beyond their saleable interest and which is not in accordance with law. The High Court Division also observed that Exhibit-1 shows Sayed son of Sarabdi Molla nad Jasim Molla son of Dabaru Mot la sold .09 acre of land out of the suit plot to one Nuki Molla by a kabala dated 12.02.1942 A.D. and Entaj Ali Molla and Kubbat Ali Molla both sons of Mohar Molla transferred .09 acre of land out of the suit plot to the said Nub Molla by a kabala dated 08.03.1948 A.D. but the plaintiff 8 did not state anything about the same in the plaint which is non disclosure of material facts which are relevant and necessary for proper adjudication of the ease between the parties. By submitting Exhibit-5 although the plaintiffs tried to show that they had purchased .14 acre of land out of the suit plot from one Most. Habljan Bibi and another Mohammad Ali on 24.01.1963 but they did not state anything about any such purchase in the plaint. Moreover, it was rightly held that there was no evidence as to how the said two vendors had interest in .14 acre of land to sell the same to the plaintiffs and as such the said Exhibit-5 is wholly unconnected with their plaint. 

 16. In respect of possession of the defendants in the suit land, the High Court Division upon going through the testimony of P.W.1 found that there was no barga kabuliyat in respect of the barga settlement to defendant No. 1. Nobody was also present at the time of talking about the said barga settlement. Hasen Ali Molla who as per his statement knew about delivery of barga crops by defendant No.1 to the plaintiffs was not examined as witness.
